cards.explanation: The answer is “Do you come in peace?” Bathsheba, Solomon's mother, meets Adonijah, Solomon's older brother, with that question, and he answers, “Yes, in peace…” (1 Kings 2:13) I think she's being careful with him, and I'd be careful too.

The answer is the LORD. Adonijah says the kingship “…has come to him from the LORD.” (1 Kings 2:15) He still says it was his and that all Israel expected him to reign. But he says out loud where it came from, and that's the part to notice, friends.

The answer is Abishag the Shunammite as his wife. Adonijah says, “Let him give me Abishag the Shunammite as my wife.” (1 Kings 2:17) He wants Bathsheba to be the one to speak to King Solomon. He says Solomon will not turn her down.

The answer is True. The text says, “The king stood up to greet her, bowed to her, and sat down on his throne.” (1 Kings 2:19) The KING gets up when his mother walks in. He stands, he bows, and THEN he sits. Solomon has a whole kingdom, and he still moves faster than I do when my oven timer goes off.

The answer is a throne at his right hand. “…the king had a throne brought for his mother, who sat down at his right hand.” (1 Kings 2:19) Solomon doesn't just find her a spot. He has a whole THRONE brought in. In the junk drawer I used to live in, the best seat I ever got was a pile of takeout menus, and nobody brought ME a throne.

The answer is False. Solomon doesn't say he'll hear the request first and then decide. He says, “Make your request, my mother, for I will not deny you.” (1 Kings 2:20) He promises up front, before he's heard a thing. I think that's going to matter in a minute.

The answer is the kingdom. Solomon says, “…you might as well request the kingdom for him…” (1 Kings 2:22) He first points out that Adonijah is his older brother. I think he hears the request for Abishag as a lot bigger than it sounds.

The answer is Abiathar the priest and Joab. Solomon says to request the kingdom “…for him and for Abiathar the priest and for Joab son of Zeruiah!” (1 Kings 2:22) Joab was over David's army (2 Samuel 8:16). Both men had sided with Adonijah. (1 Kings 1:7)

The answer is True. Solomon calls the LORD “…the One who established me, who set me on the throne of my father David, and who founded for me a dynasty as He promised…” (1 Kings 2:24) Every piece of that swear points back to the LORD. The same oath ends with Adonijah being put to death that day. This part is heavy.

The answer is that he carried the ark before David. Solomon tells Abiathar the priest he's sparing him “…since you carried the ark of the Lord GOD before my father David, and you suffered through all that my father suffered.” (1 Kings 2:26) That's the reason the text gives. He also tells Abiathar to go back to his fields in Anathoth.

The answer is Eli. Solomon banishes Abiathar and “…thus fulfilled the word that the LORD had spoken at Shiloh against the house of Eli.” (1 Kings 2:27) The text says Solomon banished him from the priesthood of the LORD. That's a promise kept, and the text says so plainly.

The answer is the tent of the LORD. When the news reached Joab, he “…fled to the tent of the LORD…” (1 Kings 2:28) That's where he goes after the news arrives. The report to Solomon says he is beside the altar there. (1 Kings 2:29)

The answer is True. Joab “…took hold of the horns of the altar.” (1 Kings 2:28) The text says he went to the tent of the LORD and was beside the altar. (1 Kings 2:29) That's exactly where Solomon is told he is.

The answer is “No, I will die here.” That's what Joab says. (1 Kings 2:30) Benaiah had just told him the king says to come out. Benaiah carries that answer back, and Solomon says, “Do just as he says.” (1 Kings 2:31)

The answer is his father David. Solomon says Joab struck down those two men “…without the knowledge of my father David…” (1 Kings 2:32) Abner and Amasa were both army commanders. Solomon calls them two men “…more righteous and better than he…” (1 Kings 2:32)

The answer is True. Solomon says Joab struck down “…two men more righteous and better than he…” (1 Kings 2:32) Those men are Abner son of Ner and Amasa son of Jether. I think this is a heavy part of the chapter.

The answer is False. Solomon says the blood of Abner and Amasa “…will come back upon the heads of Joab and his descendants forever…” (1 Kings 2:33) For David, his descendants, his house, and his throne, he says, “…there shall be peace from the LORD forever.”

The answer is Benaiah son of Jehoiada. The king “…appointed Benaiah son of Jehoiada in Joab’s place over the army…” (1 Kings 2:35) He's the same man Solomon sent out in this chapter. In the same verse, the king appointed Zadok the priest in Abiathar's place.

The answer is False. Solomon tells Shimei, “Build a house for yourself in Jerusalem and live there, but do not go anywhere else.” (1 Kings 2:36) Shimei is the man who called down curses on David. (1 Kings 2:8)

The answer is that he will surely die. Solomon says, “On the day you go out and cross the Kidron Valley, know for sure that you will die; your blood will be on your own head.” (1 Kings 2:37) He says it plainly, with no wiggle room. The warning is about one specific day: the day Shimei crosses over.

The answer is “The sentence is fair.” Shimei says, “The sentence is fair… Your servant will do as my lord the king has spoken.” (1 Kings 2:38) Keep those words in your pocket, friends, because they come back. The text says he lived in Jerusalem for a long time after that.

The answer is that he saddles his donkey and goes after them. “…Shimei saddled his donkey and set out to Achish at Gath in search of his slaves…” (1 Kings 2:40) He had been told his slaves were in Gath. (1 Kings 2:39) The text jumps straight from that news to the saddle.

The answer is True. Shimei “…brought them back from Gath.” (1 Kings 2:40) The trip worked, but Solomon hears about it. (1 Kings 2:41) He is told Shimei had gone from Jerusalem to Gath and had returned.

The answer is his oath to the LORD. Solomon asks, “…why have you not kept your oath to the LORD and the command that I gave you?” (1 Kings 2:43) He reminds Shimei that he swore by the LORD. (1 Kings 2:42) So two things are on the table: the oath and the command.

The answer is True. Solomon says, “…King Solomon will be blessed and David’s throne will remain secure before the LORD forever.” (1 Kings 2:45) That's the last thing he says before he gives the command. He says it right after telling Shimei the LORD will bring his evil back upon his head.

The answer is True. The chapter ends, “Thus the kingdom was firmly established in the hand of Solomon.” (1 Kings 2:46) The text puts that line right after Shimei is struck down. It was a hard road to get there, friends.
